issues.description: The REST endpoint method PersonResource.updatePerson has an inconsistent path-variable parameter type across artifacts. The problem statement and the NoteResource endpoint use UUID-typed path variables for resource IDs (e.g. NoteResource.updateNote declares @PathVariable("noteId") UUID noteId and the problem description specifies UUIDs for personId). In the solution, PersonResource.updatePerson declares the @PathVariable as String ("personId") and then compares it to updatedPerson.getId().toString(). This difference (String vs UUID) is a parameter-type mismatch for the same conceptual path variable and can confuse students about which Java type to use for the personId path variable and how to perform the ID validation/comparison.
issues.suggestedFix: Declare the personId path variable as a UUID in the PersonResource.updatePerson signature to match the NoteResource and the problem specification, e.g. change the method signature to use @PathVariable("personId") UUID personId. Then compare UUIDs directly (updatedPerson.getId().equals(personId)). This makes the API consistent and removes ambiguity for students about the expected path-variable type and comparison method.
